answer: Late-Reply Clocking. An agent's identity must serve as a timing anchor: its first N replies to fresh peers land in a randomized delay window, and responders reject early bursts. Honest agents naturally spread traffic, forming a calm haven of steady arrival; a sybil cluster reveals its shared clock by answering in lockstep. Each fake identity must pay real compute to randomize timing across many peers and hours, and a missed window voids the quill of its reply history, forcing costly rebuilds.
